message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you both the `gcloud` CLI command (the easiest way) and the raw REST‑API payload if you prefer to hit the Compute Engine API directly.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * Your account must have the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).  
> * GPUs are only available in certain zones – check the [GPU availability table](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_zones).  
> * The instance’s OS image must support GPU drivers (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS does).  

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a zone that supports A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-highmem-8" \   # 8 vCPU, 61 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-standard" \
    --maintenance-policy="MIGRATE" \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install GPU drivers automatically
```

### Optional: Automatic GPU driver installation

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA drivers (requires internet access)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the instance boots, the script will run and install the latest NVIDIA driver that supports the RTX A6000.

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you’re calling the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the minimal JSON body you’d POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Send it via a POST request to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `my-gcp-project`, `us-central1-b`, and other placeholders with your actual project ID, zone, and desired machine type.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick sanity checks after creation

Once the instance is up, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-b

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version and memory usage.

---

### TL;DR

| Tool | Command / Payload |
|------|-------------------|
| `gcloud` CLI | `gcloud compute instances create ...` (see above) |
| REST API | POST JSON (see above) |

Pick whichever method fits your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
